major loss of hand and wrist function due to structural damage caused by the injury.
major loss of muscle bulk of the forearm.
The right thumb was fused ... movement of the basal joint of the thumb were limited and so were the movements of the joints of other fingers.
partial loss of sensation of the fingers.
unable to use heavy tools such as drills or hammers or carry heavy weight with his right hand.
could not grip with his right hand.
could no longer use chopsticks or write properly.

treatments_received.treatment: urgent debridement and fixation of the fractures
source: Urgent debridement and fixation of the fractures were performed on the day of admission.
treatments_received.vmis_procedure: Open reduction for arm / leg / patella / scapula +/- internal fixation

source: Subsequent debridements and wound coverage were also performed thereafter.
Intensive physiotherapy and occupational therapy was given to the Plaintiff

treatments_received.treatment: regular outpatient physiotherapy and occupational therapy and follow-up treatment
source: After his discharge, the Plaintiff then received regular outpatient physiotherapy and occupational therapy and follow-up treatment.
The Plaintiff was re-admitted to the hospital on 26 June 1999 for bone grafting and was discharged on 3 July 1999.

treatments_received.treatment: correction of right thumb deformity and fusion of the interphalangeal and metacarpo-phalangeal joint of the right thumb (28 December 1999 admission)
source: The Plaintiff was again admitted to the hospital on 28 December 1999 for correction of the right thumb deformity and fusion of the interphalangeal and metacarphal-phalangeal joint of the right thumb. He was discharged on 31 December 1999. After his discharge, the Plaintiff was put on a thumb cast.
After his discharge, the Plaintiff was put on a thumb cast.

Ugly scars on the right forearm and right hand, an ugly defect on the left hip and ugly scars on the thighs causing embarrassment and a complex.
Partial loss of sensation of the fingers.
